statement: All four Metal knobs in the #162 table are value-parsed, not presence-based: each reads its env var through a helper that treats the literal "0" as off and any other non-empty value as on. The three REQUIRE spellings (session-union, IQ2 grouped-MM, exact-rows-persistent) fail closed with an error print when ineligible, but there is NO positive admission print -- no Metal analogue of CUDA's `target_admitted=1`. The only admission signal is the absence of the fail-closed error. Q4_STREAM_OVERLAP has no REQUIRE spelling at all; it is a soft opt-in via ENABLE/DISABLE only. This matters because a presence-based knob would let an 'off' arm silently run on (the adamlawi 0.0% trap); these are all value-parsed, so '0' genuinely disables.

claims.statement: All four knobs read their env var through a value-parsed helper: metal_graph_tp_env_flag (ds4.c:17835) returns dflt when unset/empty and `strcmp(env, "0") != 0` otherwise; ds4_gpu_env_bool (ds4_metal.m:3373) returns -1 when unset, 1 for 1/true/yes/on, 0 for 0/false/no/off, and treats an unrecognized value as presence-enabled with a warning; ds4_gpu_exact_rows_persistent_env_enabled (ds4_metal.m:14822) returns `value && value[0] && strcmp(value, "0") != 0`. In every case the literal "0" disables. The `strcmp(env, "0") != 0` pattern recurs across the codebase, confirming value-parsing is the norm.
claims.falsifier: If any knob reads its env var with a bare getenv() presence check (no value comparison), that knob is presence-based and the 'value-parsed' claim collapses for it.

claims.statement: There is no positive admission print for any of the four knobs: grep for 'admitted'/'target_admitted' finds no fprintf/printf that reports a REQUIRE path being selected. The REQUIRE spellings print only on failure (fail-closed).
claims.falsifier: If a positive admission print exists (a fprintf that fires when a REQUIRE path is selected), then the 'no admission print' claim collapses and the peer must use that string instead of the absence-of-error signal.

claims.statement: The three REQUIRE spellings fail closed with these exact error strings: session-union at ds4.c:73983-73988 'required Metal Q4 SSD session union is ineligible (need 2..5 valid sessions, AProjQ4 + routed IQ2_XXS/Q2_K, static decode map, and >= rows*6 cached experts)'; IQ2 grouped-MM at ds4_metal.m:50664-50669 'ds4: required Metal IQ2_XXS SSD grouped address-MM path was not selected tokens=%u gate=%u down=%u'; exact-rows-persistent at ds4_metal.m:20449-20453 'ds4: Metal exact-row persistent cache is required but disabled or ineligible (cache_budget=%u size_class_budget=%u unique=%u)'.
argv: required Metal Q4 SSD session union is ineligible

expect.stdout_contains: required Metal Q4 SSD session union is ineligible

observed.stdout: 73983:                     "required Metal Q4 SSD session union is ineligible "

claims.falsifier: If the REQUIRE spellings do not print these fail-closed errors (or print different text), the error-string claim collapses and the peer cannot rely on them as the admission signal.

claims.statement: Q4_STREAM_OVERLAP has no REQUIRE spelling: ds4_q4_stream_overlap_policy (ds4.c:71917) reads only DS4_METAL_ENABLE_Q4_STREAM_OVERLAP and DS4_METAL_DISABLE_Q4_STREAM_OVERLAP via metal_graph_tp_env_flag, both defaulting false. It is a soft opt-in with no fail-closed arm.
claims.falsifier: If a DS4_METAL_REQUIRE_Q4_STREAM_OVERLAP spelling exists, then stream-overlap does have a REQUIRE arm and the 'no REQUIRE' claim collapses.
